why: phase-379 W4. rcl asks the caller to re-supply the node at teardown (`rcl_publisher_fini(&pub, &node)`), and since phase-492 our signature is the same; the entity ALSO stores this identity instead of the `*const rcl_node_t` it used to hold, so the check below does not depend on the caller passing the right node. The PLATFORM constraint is that C gives the caller no tools to enforce the lifetime rcl's shape depends on: a node declared on an RTOS task stack dies with `vTaskDelete`, `rcl_node_t a = b;` is legal and silent, and there is no allocator to hide an indirection behind. rcl's form does not remove that assumption, it relocates it to a caller who cannot check it either. An identity CAN be checked: `rcl_node_fini` retires the slot's generation, so finalising an entity after its node returns RCLC_RET_STALE_NODE instead of succeeding silently against caller storage the runtime does not own. Generation 0 is reserved so a zeroed struct never resolves.
